subject: Network egress paths and IaC ownership for private VPC egress sequencing
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Network egress paths and IaC ownership for private VPC egress sequencing

Hi Liam —

Quick follow-up from our onboarding call this morning. We're starting the IaC review for the private deployment footprint and I want to lock down the egress/egress-proxy ownership and the CI gate expectations before the first Terraform/Helm PRs land. Specific asks: 

- Could you confirm whether Acme will keep NAT/egress as provider-managed (central NAT gateways) or if you prefer per-environment managed NAT (customer-owned)?
- Do you have an authoritative egress diagram we should use for the terraform module interface (route tables/NAT/proxies)?
- We're proposing the following split (draft): terraform/priv-vpc (network/topology) owned by Acme network team; terraform/priv-egress (egress proxies, NAT integration) owned by Redwood Ops; helm/edge-proxy chart owned by Redwood Apps. CI: we want a preflight pipeline job that runs a dryplan + e2e connectivity smoke test before apply.

Attached: initial proposed module split (proposed-module-split.patch) and a sample helm-values file for the edge proxy (helm-values-sample.yaml). Also linked the onboarding ticket JIRA SUP-2345 for context.

Can you confirm the NAT preference and whether the network diagram you mentioned during the call is shareable? If provider-managed, we'll scope terraform/priv-egress to interface points only. If customer-managed, we'll include nat-gateway creations and nat route propagation in the module.

Thanks,
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: proposed-module-split.patch (text/patch), helm-values-sample.yaml (text/yaml)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, EdgeNet Ops <ops@edgenet.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Network egress paths and IaC ownership for private VPC egress sequencing

David,

Thanks — good summary. Acme's current production pattern uses a centralized pair of NAT gateways in each region and an egress proxy cluster sitting behind them (we do this to maintain centralized egress logging and DLP). We'll send the network diagram as a PDF; attaching the topology we referenced.

Two quick notes:
1) We'd prefer provider-managed NAT gateways (centralized) — Acme network team will own the actual NAT gateway resources.
2) For the egress proxy, we want the helm chart to accept a list of allowed outbound CIDR ranges (we manage outbound approvals).

If Redwood's suggested split maps terraform/priv-vpc to our network team and terraform/priv-egress to Redwood, that's reasonable. We'll need a clear runbook for DNS and private route updates since we tie our egress proxies into internal service discovery.

I'll loop in EdgeNet Ops to confirm any peering/AS path constraints. Attaching: acme-egress-diagram.pdf.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Cloud Platform Lead, Acme Cloud
---
Attachments: acme-egress-diagram.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Network egress paths and IaC ownership for private VPC egress sequencing

Liam —

Appreciate the diagram. Quoting your key points inline: 

> Acme's current production pattern uses a centralized pair of NAT gateways in each region and an egress proxy cluster sitting behind them (we do this to maintain centralized egress logging and DLP).

Got it — that aligns with provider-managed NAT. Based on that, here's what we propose (concrete):

- Ownership (proposed):
  - terraform/priv-vpc: Acme network team — defines VPC CIDRs, subnets, route tables, peering, and NAT gateway attachments.
  - terraform/priv-egress: Redwood Ops — defines the integration glue (route table associations for proxies, security group rules to allow proxy egress to approved ranges, index of proxy endpoints used by apps).
  - helm/edge-proxy chart: Redwood Apps team — chart supports allowed_outbound_cidrs (values.egress.allowedCidrs) and chart hooks for readiness/liveness checks.
  - ansible/security jobs: Redwood Security — bastion patching, OS hardening, and cron-based cert rotation.

- CI/CD expectations: 
  - GitLab: each repo must have: terraform fmt + validate in a pre-merge job, an 'iactest-dryplan' job that runs in a ephemeral sandbox (namespace) and a pipeline 'connectivity-smoke' stage that runs an ingress/egress probe to the Acme proxy endpoint before awarding an apply gate.
  - PR checklist: owner approval (Acme for priv-vpc), a security review (auto for s2s rules), and a smoke test artifact (pass/fail).

Action items for Acme (please confirm):
1) Confirm you want provider-managed NAT (you already said yes; marking as accepted)
2) Share the list of allowed outbound CIDRs (we will map these to helm-values.allowedCidrs)
3) Confirm any peering/AS path constraints (EdgeNet ops) — any blacklisted ASNs?

I attached a quick patch with the proposed module interface (proposed-module-split.patch) and a small iac-diff highlighting the route-table variables we will need (iac-diff.patch). If that interface looks good, we'll open the initial PRs and set up the pipeline template.

On the CI smoke test — Karthik and Kimberly, can you confirm we have capacity to run the ephemeral sandbox in the shared staging cluster (kubestage-1) during PR checks?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Staff Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: proposed-module-split.patch (text/patch), iac-diff.patch (text/patch)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeNet Ops <ops@edgenet.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T18:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Network egress paths and IaC ownership for private VPC egress sequencing

Irene, David —

Thanks for the clear split. Confirmations below: 

- Confirmed: provider-managed NAT gateways (Acme network owns NAT resources).
- Allowed outbound CIDRs: sending that list to ops@edgenet.com (they'll share the canonical file).
- No blacklisted ASNs for peering at the moment; EdgeNet Ops will confirm any route-map constraints tomorrow.

Request: please include a firewall rule in terraform/priv-egress to allow outbound telemetry (TCP 443) to our security collector at 10.12.0.200/32 — we treat telemetry as a first-class flow.

If you can add that rule to the proposed iac-diff and kick off the initial PRs, we can schedule the runbook handoff next week. Procurement will track the contract-side deliverables.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Cloud Platform Lead, Acme Cloud
